title: Troubleshooting Primer
scenario: Welcome to Troubleshooting Primer. Before proceeding, you must master these essential networking terms. Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP): Ports 67 (server) / 68 (client). UDP. Assigns IP, subnet mask, gateway, DNS via DORA (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge). Option 3 = gateway, Option 6 = DNS. Address Resolution Protocol (ARP): Resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses on a local network. Broadcast request, unicast reply. ARP cache stores mappings. Vulnerable to ARP poisoning — mitigated by DAI. Domain Name System (DNS): Port 53 (UDP for queries, TCP for zone transfers). Resolves hostnames to IP addresses. NXDOMAIN = name doesn't exist. Poisoning mitigated by DNSSEC. Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP): Layer 3 protocol for error reporting and diagnostics. Used by ping (echo request/reply) and traceroute (TTL exceeded). Not for data transfer. ICMP redirect, unreachable, time exceeded messages.
question: What does DHCP stand for?
explanation: DHCP stands for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
